He would also ensure that he sent the plate of (his daughter) Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) last so that if there are any defects, it would be in her share (and none could accuse him of nepotism). He then put some of the camel's meat into these plates and sent them to the wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Thereafter, he gave instructions for the remaining meat to be cooked. When it was cooked, he invited the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar to partake of it."[^1]
Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) Feeds People
The Practice of Hadhrat Talha (RA) and the Statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ in this Regard

Hadhrat Salama bin Akwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) purchased a well at the foot of a mountain, he invited people for a meal. It was then that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "You, O Talha, are 'Fayyaadh' (an extremely generous person)."[^2]
Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abu Taalib (RA) Feeds People
The Narration of Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "The person who most benefited the poor was Ja'far bin Abu Taalib (RA). He would take us home and feed us with whatever he had in his house. In fact, (when there was nothing) he would break open the butter container so that we could lick whatever butter remained."[^3]
The Incident of Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) with Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) says, "I prepared some food for Rasulullaah ﷺ and went to (invite) him whilst he sat amongst a group of Sahabah (RA). I stood in front of him and gestured to him (to come to eat). He gestured back to ask whether the others could also join us. When I indicated that they could not, he remained silent. I remained standing where I was. When Rasulullaah ﷺ again looked my way, I gestured yet again (for him to come eat). For the second time, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked whether the others could join us and again I repeated
Maalik, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.1 Pg.296).
